extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and petitioners seeking to request EPA rulemaking or to learn about petition procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and informational landing page about citizen petitions to the U.S. EPA for rulemaking (administrative petitions and petitions under environmental statutes), and where petition records are made available by EPA offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition under the APA
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), federal agencies must give interested persons the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the basis for administrative petitions for rulemaking; the page links to further information ("Explore Administrative Petitions").

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of petitions is informational only
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provides certain information on various types of petitions in the interest of sharing information about requests the agency has received. The agency does not control the content or timing of petitions it receives and the posting of these petitions does not indicate a decision to grant or deny them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explanatory limitation: publication of a petition on EPA's site is not an agency action or a grant/denial, but a disclosure of received requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory actions following a petition remain subject to outreach and notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any regulatory action that follows as a result of a petition for rulemaking would still be shaped by the typical outreach used by the agency to gather stakeholder input, and is still subject to any applicable notice and comment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a petition prompts regulatory activity, the normal rulemaking processes (stakeholder outreach; notice-and-comment) apply before any regulatory change is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under environmental statutes and availability of judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is governed by many environmental statutes, such as the Clean Air Act (CAA) or Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA). Citizens may file petitions for review in courts to challenge actions taken by EPA under these statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes administrative petitions under the APA from statutory petitions and indicates that statutory schemes may provide judicial-review pathways; the page points readers to further information ("Explore Environmental Statute Petitions").

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-specific petition records availability (OAR, OCSPP, OLEM, OW)
rubrics_metrics.description: This site provides pages that make available petitions for rulemaking received by specific EPA offices (Office of Air and Radiation; Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention; Office of Land and Emergency Management; Office of Water) on or after January 1, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each office has a separate listing ("Explore OAR Petitions", "Explore OCSPP Petitions", "Explore OLEM Petitions", "Explore OW Petitions"); the date threshold for availability is stated as on or after January 1, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting EPA about petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact Us about Petitions to ask a question, provide feedback, or report a problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page identifies a contact pathway for questions, feedback, or reporting issues related to petitions.
